summary: San Bernardino NF knob lookout: built 1934/37, destroyed in the 1936 Etiwanda fire, replaced 1937; foundations and melted glass remain, reached by a forest road and brushy trail.

facts.design: 10-foot steel tower with a 14-foot square cab (1937 replacement)
facts.agency: US Forest Service, San Bernardino National Forest
facts.status_note: The register gives no removal date. A 2025 trip report and a summit page describe foundations and melted glass on the knob.

access.note: Free parking on Forest Road 1N34, which a 2025 trip report describes as gated and open seasonally. The same report says the road was about to close for the summer and reopen in September. No site-level rule appears in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: About 2 miles round trip on an overgrown use trail from Forest Road 1N34, per a 2025 trip report; the writer found the road needed a 4x4

events.note: Register 'Built' field reads 1934/37; a March 1934 paper reports a lookout tower as planned work on San Sevaine ridge
Etiwanda fire in the fall of 1936
Original tower destroyed; its two occupants escaped down a firebreak (report dated October 2, 1936)
Lookout Oliver O. Mittman was one of the two occupants when the tower was destroyed
Replacement 10-foot steel tower built under the San Bernardino forest building engineer
Glenn E. Downer resigned as lookout to take a state lookout job on Gilman Peak; Raymond R. Higgins was to replace him

resolved_conflicts.explanation: SummitPost describes a 10-foot timber tower dated 1935. The 1937 newspaper report, quoted on Forest Lookouts, says the replacement has a 10-foot steel tower, and the register gives steel for the 1937 structure. We treat the steel tower as the 1937 replacement.

notes_for_editor: History rests on the register and newspaper items quoted on the Forest Lookouts site; the 1936 fire date is the October 2, 1936 newspaper date, not a confirmed fire date. Today's remains and the access picture come from a 2025 hiker's trip report and a summit page, not an official source. Access is marked restricted: the 2025 trip report describes a seasonal gate on Forest Road 1N34 and a summer closure, and no site-level rule was found; a Forest Service check before any visit would settle the current status. Record height_m 3.0 is consistent with the 10-foot tower. The summit page's 1935 timber-tower claim is noted but not adopted.
